chooseBacking.title: Hook & loop or PSA: choose the right backing
chooseBacking.intro: The attachment system is as important as the grit. Match it to the pad before you order.

start.title: Start with the requirement
start.body: Hook & loop discs mount onto a compatible hook-faced pad and suit operations where grit is changed often. PSA discs rely on pressure-sensitive adhesive and need a clean, flat pad. The two systems are not interchangeable.

compat.title: Confirm compatibility
compat.body: Confirm pad diameter, backing type and dust-extraction layout. A non-hole disc does not connect to a hole-based extraction pattern, and open-mesh discs need a compatible pad and extraction system.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: Include disc diameter, backing, grit list, quantity per grit and workpiece material. Ask for a sample evaluation before approving a production order.

beltChecklist.title: What to include in an abrasive belt enquiry
beltChecklist.intro: A clear specification helps your supplier review fit and prepare a useful quotation.

start.title: Start with the requirement
start.body: Give the belt length and width in millimetres. Name the machine model — a machine specification sheet or a photo of an old belt label helps.

compat.title: Confirm compatibility
compat.body: Add workpiece material, preferred abrasive, grit, backing requirement and joint requirements. Avoid selecting a product using belt colour alone.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: List quantities by size and grit, packaging preferences, destination and the required delivery date. The final quotation confirms specification, availability, payment terms and transport arrangements.

gritSequence.title: Planning a grit sequence for surface preparation
gritSequence.intro: Start with the workpiece and required finish, then evaluate a sequence on a sample.

start.title: Start with the requirement
start.body: Coarse grits remove material quickly and leave deep scratches; fine grits refine the surface. The starting point depends on the substrate, defect depth and removal requirement.

compat.title: Confirm compatibility
compat.body: Step down grits in order and inspect the workpiece at each stage. Skipping grits leaves scratches that are hard to remove, and cleaning between stages avoids coarse-grit contamination.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: Grit numbering is not interchangeable between grading systems. Confirm the grading standard, abrasive type and availability in the quotation, and follow machine and abrasive safety instructions.

dustCollection.title: Dust collection & pad compatibility, explained
dustCollection.intro: Hole patterns, open-mesh discs and backer pads must match your extraction setup.

start.title: Start with the requirement
start.body: Identify your pad: number of holes, diameter and whether it is used with dust extraction. Non-hole discs and open-mesh discs behave differently from multi-hole discs.

compat.title: Confirm compatibility
compat.body: Match disc hole layout to pad ports. Open-mesh discs need a compatible pad and a working extraction system; PSA discs need a clean pad face.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: List pad model, hole count, disc size and grit list, plus your dust-extraction arrangement. Confirm sample behaviour before a production order.

oemPackaging.intro: A complete brief keeps artwork, labels and cartons on schedule.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: Attach artwork, specify pack quantities and carton marks, and state destination and timing. Sample approval comes before production.

gritStandards.title: Grit standards: FEPA, ANSI and what your list means
gritStandards.intro: Grading systems are not interchangeable — name the standard in every enquiry.

start.title: Start with the requirement
start.body: FEPA (ISO 848) and the older ANSI scale number similar sizes differently; a P120 and a 120-grit are not always the same. Name the standard you buy to.

compat.title: Confirm compatibility
compat.body: Confirm grading standard, abrasive type and availability per grade in the quotation. Do not mix grading systems in one grit list.

enquiry.title: Prepare your enquiry
enquiry.body: State the standard (e.g. FEPA P60–P800), quantity per grade and destination. Confirm the final grade list with the quotation before ordering.

alum.def: The most common abrasive grain for belts and discs: tough, workable, suited to metal, wood and general finishing.

ansi.def: Legacy North American grit numbering. Similar-size grains differ from the FEPA scale — name the standard in every enquiry.

backing-cloth.def: A cotton/cloth web that carries the abrasive grain on belts. Weight (e.g. X-weight) sets flexibility and load capacity.

backing-poly.def: Poly-cotton web backing: a balance of strength and flexibility for general-purpose belts.

belt.def: A continuous loop of abrasive grain on a web backing, used on belt machines for grinding, finishing and deburring.

blend.def: Smoothing a weld so it blends into the surrounding metal — typically a first pass on a flap disc or belt, then finer grits.

closed.def: A close-coated grain layout with little open space; the belt resists clogging on harder work.

debur.def: Removing burrs and small protrusions left by cutting, sawing or grinding.

dust.def: Removing abrasive dust at the workpiece — via pad ports, open-mesh discs or local extraction.

flap.def: A disc of overlapping abrasive flaps, flexible, for grinding, blending and finishing on angle grinders.

fepa.def: The ISO 848 (FEPA) grading scale in P-notation (e.g. P120). The default scale in most European and international trade.

grit.def: The nominal grain size of an abrasive: higher numbers are finer. Belts 40–800; discs 60–5000.

hookloop.def: The hook-and-loop attachment system for discs: the disc snaps onto a hook-faced pad.

mesh.def: Open-mesh discs have cut-out windows for dust to pass through, needing a compatible pad and extraction.

moq.def: Minimum order quantity — comes with the offer, alongside availability and terms.

oem.def: Original equipment manufacturing / private label: our products under your brand, labels and packaging.

psa.def: Pressure-sensitive adhesive backing: the disc sticks directly onto a compatible pad.

disc.def: A flat or flapped abrasive circle mounted on a pad for sanding and finishing.

sic.def: Silicon carbide grain: very hard, sharp, suited to glass, ceramics and non-ferrous metals.

prep.def: Getting a surface ready for coating or finishing: removing rust, filler or old finish to a consistent profile.

wetdry.def: Grades that stay cool and clog-resistant in wet or wet/dry use; confirm suitability with the quotation.

xweight.def: A mid-weight cloth backing for general-purpose belts: strong yet flexible.

zirconia.def: Zirconia alumina grain: tough and aggressive for metal grinding, deburring and finishing on steel.

pad.def: The backing plate a disc sits on: pad diameter, face (hook) and port layout must match the disc.
